messages:
maya: quick check — on the new quant-13B int4 bring-up i'm seeing a consistent amplitude/phase drift in early tokens when a long anchored system prompt (~1k tokens) is used. looks like rotary scaling might be off. anyone seen this with recent quant kernels?
kevin-ml: can you paste a tiny repro and whether it's deterministic across runs?
maya: deterministic across seeds and runs. minimal repro below (shortened):
```
SYS: <ANCHOR repeated 1000 tokens>
USER: What is the first word of the system anchor?
EXPECTED: <anchor content>
OBSERVED: shifted wording, token probs re-weighted near start
```
eli: that pattern smells like a RoPE amplitude mismatch (sign/scale shift) — we've hit that before when per-head scaling got folded into quant params. what's the quant config you used?
maya: exported with export_v2, quant_mode=int4_perchannel, scale_bias=true, clip_threshold=2.5. export script: `./export --model foo --quant int4 --per-channel`
zara: try disabling per-head scaling as a quick check. also check if the fused rotary kernel (fused_rotary_v2) was selected by the runtime for int4 — we've seen it behave differently.
infra-bot: CI job 7892: longprompt-suite run finished — perf stable, quality regression detected: rouge -5% on longprompt-suite. https://ci.internal/7892
kevin-ml: if it's deterministic, bisecting kernels should be straightforward. hypothesis: when we quantize we move the rotary scale inside the integer matmul path, changing order of ops so the effective scale on cos/sin gets altered. try multiplying rotary by global scalar before quantization as a sanity check.
maya: running a small bisect now: float32 kernel vs quantized fused kernels, also will run job with per-head scaling disabled. kicking off reproduce job.
ops-bot: Reproducer job started (job id: repro-1719123469)
eli: another angle: check cast order around `apply_rotary` -> if casting to int before adding KV cached offsets we can lose subtle scaling. also check whether rotary precomputation uses float32 vs a reduced precision path in quant build.
maya: plan: 1) compare float32 vs quantized outputs at token level for first 128 tokens, 2) test with per-head scaling off, 3) run kernel-variant A/B (fused_rotary_v1 vs fused_rotary_v2) under same weight blobs, 4) add unit test in runtime to assert amplitude match within 1e-3 for anchored prompts.
kevin-ml: if you confirm deterministic drift, add a small regression test in `tests/rotary/anchored_amplitude` and mark it flaky=false so infra alerts.
zara: :thumbsup: i'll prep the longprompt-suite slice and flag failing examples for triage.
maya: update: repro job logs show the drift only when context > 512 and anchor tokens present; shorter anchors don't reproduce. sharing logs shortly.
ops-bot: Reproducer job finished (repro-1719123469): status=failed-quality, diffstat attached in CI.
maya: thanks — will follow up with bisect results and a PR once we pin the kernel. leaving notes here for whoever picks it up.
